newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Newmont Uzbek gold project at full capacity end-96.
newsitem.headline: Newmont Uzbek gold project at full capacity end-96.

text.p: U.S.-based Newmont Mining Corp's Zarafshan Newmont gold project in Uzbekistan will reach full production of one tonne per month by December 1996, the director of Newmont (Uzbekistan) Ltd said on Wednesday.
"We're debugging the system at the moment -- but these are the last steps which are always the hardest," Director Dennis Erwin told Reuters in the Uzbek capital Tashkent.
He said the venture, between Newmont Mining and the Uzbek government, is currently producing 800-900 kg of gold a month. All production is shipped to London.

Newmont is reprocessing low-grade waste ore at the Muruntau mine, located around 400 km west of Tashkent in the Kyzylkum desert. Production began in May 1995, with the project expected to last 18 years.
He said cash costs were currently about $200-205 per ounce of gold.
Trade journals say the Central Asian nation of 22 million is the world's ninth largest gold producer, with output last year of 63.6 tonnes.
